title: DVR Labs Boarding Pass - Split-Flap Ticker & Perforated Tear-Off Stub

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: Airport split-flap departure boards flipping characters; a paper boarding pass with radial notches and a tear-off stub along a perforation line that gives resistance before ripping raggedly.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: Airport codes and gate rendered as split-flap tiles: on change each tile's top half falls and bottom half rises via Web Animations API, tiles staggered a beat apart, gate changes flagged in accent color. Dragging the stub along the perforation makes the paper flex, then tear along a ragged clip-path edge and fall with the user's throw; Reprint restores it.

design_tokens.borders: Paper perforation via radial-gradient notch masks; hairline ticket rules; ragged clip-path tear edge
design_tokens.elevation: Subtle paper depth (slight shadow/flex on drag), tiles flat; on tall screens the pass rotates upright
design_tokens.typography: Monospaced condensed ticket type with per-letter split-flap tiles; bold seat/gate numerals; functional label-value rows like printed ticket fields

interactive_mechanics: Drag the stub along the perforation - elastic paper give, ragged tear, stub falls away with throw physics
Split-flap letter flip animations with staggered timing on any code/gate change
Settings panel re-generates route/gate and replays flips; live QR code encoded from route/seat/gate as one SVG path
Auto-play flips until first user touch
usability_notes: Shows micro-interactions suited to travel and booking components; the tear-off affordance doubles as a satisfying 'confirm/done' gesture. Risks: tear gesture needs a visible affordance hint and a keyboard/reduced-motion fallback; split-flap animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion; notches and ragged edges reduce scan-column alignment, so keep data rows outside the perforation zone.
